q: How faithful must the doubling-schedule stopping-time model be to preserve the O(kappa log^3 kappa) scaling when the eigenvalue density deviates from geometric (e.g., a heavy-tailed distribution near lambda=1/kappa)?
basis: In the toy Statevector reproduction the geometric branch-mass p_i ~ 1/4^i was CHOSEN to make T_av bounded; when we changed to uniform p_i (the first attempt) T_av grew like sqrt(kappa) and the VTAA advantage collapsed. Ambainis's proof implicitly assumes eigenvalues are distributed such that the amortized T_av stays polylog. Real Ax=b instances (e.g. discretized elliptic PDEs) have known non-geometric spectral densities; the exponent of the resulting quantum speedup is not spelled out in the paper.
next_steps: Sweep p_i distributions (uniform, geometric with varying ratio, power-law tails) at a small fixed kappa in the same Qiskit Statevector harness and fit the effective exponent of Q_variable vs kappa. Cross-reference with condensed-matter spectra from real HHL benchmarks (e.g. Cade et al.'s Poisson-equation solves) to see whether the O(kappa*polylog) prediction actually holds.

q: What is the smallest kappa at which the VTAA advantage exceeds the constant-factor overhead of nesting Aaronson-Ambainis Lemma 1 log(kappa) times deep?
basis: The Statevector sweep shows that for kappa<=64 in the HHL-regime experiment, Q_standard is actually SMALLER than Q_variable (speedup 0.6 -> 0.97). Crossover happens near kappa~64-128. Ambainis's constants are not tight enough in the paper to predict this crossover exactly; our fit puts it at kappa* ~ 90 in the toy model.
next_steps: Analytically bound the constant in front of T_max*log(T_max) in Theorem 1 (paper hides it in the O()). Then repeat the sweep with proper Aaronson-Ambainis Lemma-1 (2m+1)-repetition constants baked in and measure the true crossover in a resource-count sense (T gates, not just 'query proxy').

q: Does the variable-time amplitude *estimation* subroutine that A' invokes (Theorem 4, Estimate(A,c,p,k)) itself require modification to inherit the O(kappa) improvement, or does the standard estimation already suffice as a black box?
basis: Section 3.2 uses Estimate as a black box that costs sqrt(1+loglog(1/p))/max(eps,p) per call. But when applied to Bᵢ (which itself has variable stopping times), the effective sample cost per estimation call inherits T_max, not T_av. The paper's amortization is not written out explicitly for the estimation subroutine; my Qiskit implementation could not distinguish the two because I did not simulate Estimate at all.
next_steps: Implement Ambainis's Estimate(B_i, c, 1/kappa, log m + 5) explicitly on the toy states used here, count actual A-invocations vs the Theorem-4 bound, and test whether an unmodified Estimate gives an extra log factor beyond the promised log^3 kappa.

q: What is the empirical quantum-vs-classical crossover point for the HHL-with-VTAA algorithm at practical eps~1e-3 for sparse condensed-matter A matrices, given the O(1/eps^3) dependence?
basis: Theorem 3 shows time O(C*kappa*log^3(kappa/eps) * log^2(1/eps) / eps^3). The eps^3 in the denominator is UGLY. In the reproduction I only tracked kappa-scaling with a fixed p_succ model; the eps-dependence is untested. For eps=1e-3 this factor alone is 1e9 -- swamping the kappa-linearity gain unless kappa is huge.
next_steps: Sweep eps in the toy from 1e-1 down to 1e-3, count effective queries, and compare against classical CG on the same discretized matrix (n=1024) to identify the (kappa, eps) region where quantum wins in real gate counts, not asymptotics.

q: The reproduction assumed Ambainis's Model requirement (nested Hᵢ subspaces, P_Hᵢ|ψᵢ₊₁,₀⟩ = |ψᵢ,₀⟩) holds automatically -- how brittle is VTAA when a real physical circuit only APPROXIMATELY satisfies this (e.g., due to Hamiltonian-simulation Trotter error mixing 'stopped' amplitude back into 'not-yet-stopped')?
basis: In the Statevector experiment I hardcoded amplitudes into a fresh state with `initialize()`; the consistency conditions were tautologically satisfied. In any real HHL-VTAA implementation, Trotter simulation of e^{-iHt} at branch i+1 will not exactly preserve the branch-i stopped part, introducing an off-diagonal leak whose magnitude depends on the simulation-error budget. The paper does not quantify how much slack the Theorem-1 bound has against a delta-approximate model.
next_steps: Add a controlled 'leakage' perturbation to the toy Statevector (rotate epsilon amplitude from |0>_O and |1>_O back into |2>_O between branches) and measure how p_succ, T_av, T_max drift and whether the fitted VTAA exponent moves. Derive the effective error budget required for VTAA to still beat standard AA at kappa=1024.
